newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian president urges calm, vows money back.
newsitem.headline: Albanian president urges calm, vows money back.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha, his country thrown into turmoil by the collapse of pervasive investment schemes, promised people in Europe's poorest nation on Saturday that their savings would be refunded.

Southern Albania was racked by mass demonstrations, with protesters setting fire to government buildings and attacking Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu in the town of Lushnje, 80 km (55 miles) south of Tirana.

"I call on all citizens to cool down and I assure them that we're doing our utmost to strike the right solution so that (investors) can retrieve their money as soon as possible," Berisha, looking drawn, said on state television.

The former hermitic communist Balkan nation has been ravaged by violent protests for two weeks because pyramid investment schemes collapsed after duping many people out of their life savings with promises of high returns on small investments.

Berisha, seeking to quell the violence, tried to convene a crisis meeting of parliamentary parties. But the opposition Socialists, who refused to take their seats in the legislature after a disputed general election, declined to attend.
Maqo Lakrori, a leading Socialist official, told Reuters the only way out of the crisis would be the resignation of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi's government and fresh general elections.
He said the Socialists, reformed heirs to the communists, would continue to call on the nation to protest to this end, but he said they condemned the violence.
"It is the people's right to protest peacefully against the government," Lakrori said, adding that a rally would be staged in Tirana on Sunday.

About 5,000 angry protesters surrounded Shehu, chairman of the ruling right-wing Democratic Party, in Lushnje and he was left with blood pouring down his face after a hard object struck him, a witness said.

Shehu, a close associate of Berisha, was trying to calm the situation but apparently misread the mood of the crowd. He fled to the locker room of the town soccer stadium with his bodyguards and plain-clothes policemen.
State television reported that Shehu emerged unscathed and was returning to the capital.
Albanians have reacted fiercely to the prospect of losing the money which many of them invested in pyramid schemes after selling homes, farms, livestock and other belongings.
In Berat, 40 km (25 miles) south of Lushnje, demonstrators set fire to the town hall, a police station, the prosecutor's office and court buildings, television said.
Police used batons to break up the biggest demonstration in Tirana last Sunday but appeared powerless to prevent the latest protests.
About 30 demonstrators were arrested in Lushnje on Friday and police said 29 officers were hurt. There were no immediate figures on any injuries to protesters.
Berisha's Democrats have attempted to appease investors by banning pyramid schemes, fixing 20-year prison sentences for their operators and freezing funds. Some fund managers have been arrested.

But such action has infuriated some investors, who argue that some of the money frozen in banks should rightly belong to them. They also say that if scheme operators are jailed, they will never see their cash again.
